Uses of Interface
org.smtlib.IResponse

Packages that use IResponse
Package
Description
org.smtlib
This package contains the main classes and abstract interfaces for this SMT-LIB tool; the tool provides a stand-alone SMT-LIB-compliant command-line application, an application that responds to SMT-LIB commands over a network port, and an SMT-LIB Java API.
org.smtlib.command
This package contains implementations of the SMT-LIB commands, implementing the interfaces defined in ICommand; these implementations are independent of the concrete syntax that might be used, except that each command object has methods that can parse or print representations of the command in the standard (or potentially other) concrete syntaxes.
org.smtlib.ext
This package contains commands that are extensions to SMT-LIB.
org.smtlib.impl
This package is an implementation of the interfaces defined in org.smtlib.
org.smtlib.sexpr
This package is a concrete implementation of a particular concrete syntax for the abstract SMT-LIB semantics.
org.smtlib.solvers
This package implements various instances of org.smtlib.ISolver, which are specific solvers that wrap and interact with various off-the-shelf SMT solvers currently available.

    IAttributeValue
    This interface represents the general class of attribute values; that is, it is the super-interface of any class that may be an attribute value; in the abstract syntax it has no particular structure, though it does include true, false, string literals, numerals, and various pre-defined constants.

    Solver_simplify.check_sat_assuming(IExpr... exprs)
    check-sat-assuming postdates Simplify by well over a decade (added in SMT-LIB 2.6; Simplify's protocol has no concept of it), and this class has no override for it -- without one, it silently inherits Solver_test's stub (this class's superclass, the type-check-only pseudo-solver), which never talks to the real Simplify process at all and just echoes back whatever :status a script happened to declare (or "unknown" if none), regardless of whether the assumed literals are actually satisfiable.

    Solver_bitwuzla.get_option(IExpr.IKeyword key)
    Answered entirely client-side (never forwarded -- see class comment point 1): from whatever this run has set via Solver_bitwuzla.set_option_impl(org.smtlib.IExpr.IKeyword, org.smtlib.IAttributeValue), falling back to the standard SMT-LIB default for any option never set, and "unsupported" for anything not a recognized standard option at all (matching what a compliant solver would say about an option it doesn't have).

    Solver_bitwuzla.set_info(IExpr.IKeyword key, IAttributeValue value)
    Bitwuzla's own set-info silently accepts anything, including the reserved, implementation-defined keys (:name/:authors/:version/:error-behavior/etc.) that Solver_bitwuzla.get_info(org.smtlib.IExpr.IKeyword) always answers from its own hardcoded values regardless of what a script tries to set -- forwarding a set-info for one of those to the process would come back "success", which is misleading (it looks like it took effect; get-info would still report the fixed value right after).
